reasoning_traces.think:
The PART framework constructs ARS through a weighted linear combination of four sub-models: wellness, injury risk, physical capability, and playing style. The weights (0.35, 0.30, 0.35) and style multipliers (1.0–1.6) are learned heuristically. This is a dualized ensemble approach where each sub-model contributes to a scalar readiness score. The mathematical structure implies a convex combination of bounded indices, which can be interpreted as a belief function over athlete readiness. In GSI, this maps to Bayesian inference over latent wellness states, where ARS becomes a posterior mean. In GSE, it becomes a state vector in a readiness dynamical system. The framework fails when sub-models are not independent or when style multipliers are not representative of actual performance variation. The use of self-reported injury labels introduces a confounding bias that limits predictive validity.
